Subject: Follow-up: deployment fit + SSO / KMS / log retention (ZenWell POC)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum toward the POC: 

High-level takeaways from call:
- Primary driver: PHI + auditability for the medication management module. ZenWell needs strong control over keys and long-term audit logs.
- Initial interest: evaluate Hosted API for speed to value, but leaning toward Dedicated or Private if KMS/HSM and logging controls don’t match requirements.
- Identity: ZenWell uses Okta with SAML 2.0 + SCIM user provisioning; single-sign-on is required for the console and for any operator/engineer access.

Open clarifying questions (need answers to decide Dedicated vs Private):
1) KMS/HSM: do you require FIPS-certified on-prem HSM, or is cloud BYOK (AWS KMS CMKs) acceptable if we provide CMEK semantics?
2) Audit/log retention: you mentioned retaining logs for 7 years — is that strict (regulatory) or targetable? Also need format: immutable tamper-evident audit trail vs standard access logs.
3) Network: will the POC need VPC peering (no internet egress) or is IP allowlist + egress ok?

Attachments: I’ve attached our one-pager that contrasts Hosted / Dedicated / Private with the typical gating checklist.

Next steps I propose:
- Priya: please confirm answers to Q1–Q3 by EOD tomorrow if possible.
- Monica: Monica to prepare a short technical note on KMS/HSM options and what we’d need for a Private deployment.
- Marissa / Jonas: we’ll draft a scoping statement and ballpark pricing for Dedicated vs Private pending your answers.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from security/compliance: 

Q1 (KMS/HSM):
- Our baseline requirement is BYOK with support for rotation and customer-controlled key lifecycle. AWS KMS CMKs are acceptable for initial evaluation only if keys are under our account and you support CMK usage for model encryption and disk encryption.
- For production (post-POC), we will likely require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or better). If the Private option requires an on-prem HSM, we need to know the supported HSM vendors and the integration method (PKCS#11 / KMIP).

Q2 (audit/log retention):
- Retention: 7 years is our compliance target for audit logs relating to PHI access. Immutable/tamper-evident storage is preferred (WORM or equivalent).
- Scope: we need request-level audit trails (who called the model, which model/version, request metadata, token counts) plus system-level logs (instance lifecycle, config changes).

Q3 (network):
- For POC we can do IP allowlist + VPN, but for production we will require VPC peering or Private deployment (no public egress) depending on key management approach.

Also: can you share your most recent SOC 2 or equivalent evidence? I saw the SOC2 snapshot attachment — please confirm it is the latest.

Priya Singh
Head of Security & Compliance, ZenWell Health
priya.singh@zenwell.ai

Thanks Priya — answering with what we can provide today and what would require Private deployment / additional work: 

KMS/HSM options (short):
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood-managed keys (default). No BYOK. Not suitable if you insist on keys in your account or HSM-backed keys.
- Dedicated: Supported with BYOK via AWS KMS when Dedicated is hosted in your VPC or dedicated tenancy; you can supply CMKs in your AWS account and we can configure CMEK for storage and model artifact encryption. HSM-backed keys via cloud HSM are possible (AWS CloudHSM) — requires customer provisioning and permissions.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full BYOK and direct HSM integrations supported. We’ve integrated via PKCS#11 with common HSM vendors (SafeNet/Lunasa/YubiHSM, vendor-dependent). Private gives you the strongest guarantees and local control for key lifecycle.

Audit & logs:
- We can export request-level audit logs to your SIEM (syslog, Splunk, S3) with configurable retention. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide 365-day default retention; Dedicated can be extended via exports to your storage for longer retention (you control retention policy).
- Private: logs can remain in your environment with WORM if you supply the storage target; we support signed, append-only log exports to S3 with object lock for immutability.

Network / access:
- POC options: IP allowlist + VPN is fine for now. For production with BYOK/HSM, we recommend Private or VPC peering.

Action items from Redwood side:
- I’ll attach an internal tech note (short) describing the BYOK setup steps and the required IAM roles/permissions for AWS KMS/CloudHSM.
- Marissa / Jonas: if ZenWell confirms HSM requirement for production, we’ll scope Private and provide a checklist for on-prem/network and HSM vendor requirements.

Estimated blockers we should call out now:
- If ZenWell requires hardware HSM in your data center (air-gapped), that moves us to an on-prem Private engagement with longer lead times for packaging and validation.
- Long-term log retention with immutability requires you to host the retention store or accept cross-account S3 with object-lock plus audit controls.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-kms-integration-notes.pdf]
